The Many Faces of the Crypt Keeper: Every Version From 1949 to 2026 🧟

carousel // Sep 30, 2026

Read more on Threads

Y'all. The Crypt Keeper is BACK. 🧟

He's hosting AMC FearFest on AMC and AMC+ starting October 1, in what AMC is calling his first new segments in 30 years. So I went digging and tracked down every version of him I could find, from 1949 to 2026: the comic-book hermit, the '89 HBO puppet, dime-store masks, fan-built busts, a mask signed "Crypt Keeper"... and one imposter who thought he'd slide in unnoticed. 👀

Here are the many faces of the Keeper, slide by slide.

Slide 1: The HBO puppet vs. the FearFest puppet

Same ghoul, 37 years apart. On the left is Kevin Yagher's original puppet, first seen on HBO on June 10, 1989, the night Tales from the Crypt premiered. On the right is the 2026 version: Greg Nicotero rebuilt Yagher's puppet at his KNB EFX shop for FearFest's 30th anniversary.

Nicotero kept everything fans remember: the decaying face, the missing nose, the icy blue eyes and the rotten grin. He re-sculpted and repainted it to hold up in 4K and gave the hands more movement. And John Kassir is back on the voice, cackle and all.

Slide 2: Drawn vs. dime-store

Before he was a puppet, he was a drawing. The Crypt Keeper first showed up in EC Comics' Crime Patrol #15, cover-dated December 1949 to January 1950, hosting "Return from the Grave!", EC's first horror story. Back then he was a gaunt, wild-haired old hermit, not a corpse. He even still had his whole nose. The horror stories did so well that the book was renamed The Crypt of Terror, and then Tales from the Crypt. The mask on the left is based on that original comic look.

By the early '90s, kids were wearing him on an elastic strap: a vacuform plastic Halloween mask with cartoon paint.

Slide 3: The '90s Halloween aisle

Two latex masks from the '90s. The tan one is an unsold retail mask with the tag still on. The blue-gray one with the yellow hair has brighter skin and red lips, and it might be a custom repaint.

Store-bought masks always exaggerated the fangs and the colors, but they kept what makes him him: the rotted nose and the wild eyes.

Slide 4: Deluxe collector masks

These were made to display, not just to wear. On the left is a Halloween-Mask.com exclusive mask-bust with a brown tunic and red scarf. On the right is a collector-grade full-bust latex mask with shoulders. Both have a wider, meaner grin than the TV puppet ever had.

Slide 5: The deep cuts

Yes, the dreadlocked Keeper is real. The horror movie Ritual, shot in Jamaica, came out in some countries in 2002 and went straight to DVD in the U.S. in 2006 as Tales from the Crypt Presents: Ritual, the last Crypt-branded movie. Its home video release added new Crypt Keeper intro and outro segments, with dreadlocks and a Jamaican accent. It's one of the strangest looks he's ever had. So technically, these were the last new Crypt Keeper segments before FearFest. I get why nobody counts them.

The tuxedo Keeper is the mystery. The tux is classic Crypt Keeper, but I can't verify where this puppet photo comes from. If you know, tell me. You're a legend.

Slide 6: Fans rebuilt him first

Long before AMC called, fan artists were already rebuilding Kevin Yagher's 1989 puppet, wrinkle by wrinkle. The bust on the left is a screen-accurate replica, the closest match to the 1989–1996 TV puppet: the robe, the hair, the sunken nose. The one on the right is an independent artist's display bust, with a full neck and browner skin.

Slide 7: One of these isn't him

Did you spot it? The left one is a high-detail HBO replica bust, lit green for the mood. The right one is the imposter: stitched scalp, big teeth, big ears and no rotted nose. It's a generic zombie mask.

Slide 8: Worn and signed

On the left, that's me, in an HBO-style latex mask with glossy blue-purple custom paint. On the right is a mask signed "Crypt Keeper," which is how John Kassir usually signs. I haven't verified that signature, so treat it as unconfirmed.

From fan-worn to Kassir-signed, he's still everybody's favorite ghoul.

Catch him on AMC FearFest

The Crypt Keeper is hosting AMC FearFest all October on AMC and AMC+. It's FearFest's 30th anniversary, with more than 650 hours of horror, including marathons of A Nightmare on Elm Street and Halloween. In the new segments, he trades the classic tux for a copper smoking jacket and DJs turntables in a crypt bar full of skulls.

Sources: iHorror, CBR, Bleeding Cool, Wikipedia: Tales from the Crypt (comics)), Wikipedia: Ritual (2002 film))

Quick answers

When does the Crypt Keeper come back? He's hosting AMC FearFest on AMC and AMC+ starting October 1, 2026, in his first new segments in about 30 years.

Who voices the Crypt Keeper on AMC FearFest? John Kassir, the same voice from HBO's Tales from the Crypt.

Who made the new Crypt Keeper puppet? Greg Nicotero rebuilt Kevin Yagher's original 1989 puppet at his KNB EFX shop.

When did the Crypt Keeper first appear? In EC Comics' Crime Patrol #15, cover-dated December 1949 to January 1950.

Why does the Crypt Keeper have dreadlocks in Ritual? Ritual's home video release added new Crypt Keeper segments with dreadlocks and a Jamaican accent to match the movie's Jamaican setting.

Your turn

Which version's your favorite? Drop the number, 1–8. Did you catch the imposter on slide 7? And does anybody know where the tuxedo Keeper on slide 5 came from? 'Cause I sure don't.
